clips.text: I'm still not eating the crust.
clips.script: [stubborn, small] I'm still not eating the CRUST.

clips.text: You started without me. I made a schedule on the plane. It has tabs.
clips.script: [delighted, pleased] You started without me. [proud, brisk] I made a schedule on the plane. [pleased] It has TABS.

clips.text: I said, 'Great note, Bernadette.' Then she stood there waiting for me to move them, and I opened a soda.
clips.script: [mellow, easy] i said, great note, bernadette. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, lazy, amused] then she stood there waiting for me to move them, [mellow, laid-back, low-key, unhurried, deadpan] and i opened a soda.

clips.text: I'm Grace. I'm nine. I keep the chart.
clips.script: [crisp, official] I'm Grace. I'm nine. [proud, matter-of-fact] I keep the CHART.

clips.text: I don't take bread from a man holding a salad spinner.
clips.script: [flat, scathing] I don't take bread from a man holding a SALAD SPINNER.

clips.text: He was here fifteen minutes before your cab, 3468. You'd have seen him yourself if you were ever home.
clips.script: [dry, pointed] He was here fifteen minutes before your cab, three four six eight. [flat, jabbing] You'd have seen him yourself if you were ever HOME.

clips.text: Twelve of them, and all twelve are still there. I've been standing between that pan and your father since six this morning.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, proud] Twelve of them, and all twelve are still there. [warm Long Island accent, dry, pointed] I've been standing between that pan and your FATHER since six this morning.

clips.text: AHHH! DEEDEE!
clips.script: [real scream] AHHH! Deedee!

clips.text: CAR size? Cozy Rosie, I told everybody a couch. Twenty years! I didn't want to brag!
clips.script: [thick New York accent, sharp lift, stunned] CAR size? [thick New York accent, warm, goofy, injured] Cozy Rosie, I told everybody a COUCH. Twenty years! [thick New York accent, punchline, big] I didn't want to BRAG!

clips.text: I'm not holding anything. That flame was like that when I got here.
clips.script: [airy, defensive] I'm not holding anything. [smooth, shifting blame] That flame was like that when I got here.

clips.text: Thirty-eight thousand dollars, and the porch was already crooked.
clips.script: [in unison, flat, bored, together] Thirty-eight thousand dollars, [deadpan, together] and the porch was already crooked.

clips.text: That's a quote. I'm using it.
clips.script: [gleeful, quick] That's a QUOTE. [pleased, final] I'm using it.

clips.text: Forty loaves, two at a time, forty-five minutes each. That's fifteen hours of oven, and we have nine.
clips.script: [quick, calculating] Forty loaves, two at a time, forty-five minutes each. [rising, tense] That's fifteen HOURS of oven, [flat, grim] and we have nine.

clips.text: It was a long soda.
clips.script: [mellow, deadpan] it was a long soda.

clips.text: A person! I said it was a person. What kind of car? What time? Did anybody get the license plate?
clips.script: [explosive, thrilled] A PERSON! I said it was a person. [rapid-fire, demanding] What kind of car? What time? [urgent] Did anybody get the license plate?

clips.text: Too wet. Who taught you to shape a loaf?
clips.script: [gruff, critical] Too wet. [sour, grading] Who taught you to shape a loaf?

clips.text: Chained since 1963. I have the key. Nobody has ever asked me for it.
clips.script: [flat, dry] Chained since nineteen sixty-three. [pointed, matter-of-fact] I have the key. [deadpan] Nobody has ever ASKED me for it.

clips.text: That thing took my good twelve-cup pan! I don't even put that pan in the DISHWASHER.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, shocked, loud] That thing took my good twelve-cup PAN! [warm Long Island accent, low, indignant] I don't even put that pan in the DISHWASHER.

clips.text: Hello, mud! Can we please have Deedee's muffins back? Thank you!
clips.script: [loud, friendly, very polite] Hello, mud! Can we PLEASE have Deedee's muffins back? Thank you!

clips.text: The only thing at the end of the boulevard is the old Car Barn. My father drove the night streetcar out of it.
clips.script: [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, thoughtful, gruff] The only thing at the end of the boulevard is the old Car Barn. [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, quieter, proud] My father drove the night streetcar out of it.
